findings.title: Card is far taller than its content
findings.evidence: div.rounded-xl.border is 1120×266px but its content occupies 3% of that; 200px of empty space sits under the last line. Nothing inside it needs the height, so a fixed height or min-height is probably set.
findings.fix: Remove the fixed height / min-height and let the card size to its content, or fill the space with something that earns it.
findings.citation: Lin 2004: whitespace helps comprehension when it frames content; dead space inside a container just reads as unfinished

findings.title: Nested cards
findings.fix: Cards inside cards create visual noise and excessive depth. Flatten the hierarchy — use spacing, typography, and dividers instead of nesting containers.

findings.title: Above-the-fold is visually busy
findings.evidence: Quadtree decomposition of the first screen (text and photos masked out) needs 1789 leaves (calm pages run 50–250; busy ones 600+). Whitespace share 29%, text covers 34% of the viewport.
findings.fix: Remove one thing from the first screen. Reinecke's data says people rate low- and medium-complexity pages the same and punish high complexity; the gain is all in cutting, not adding.
findings.citation: Reinecke et al. CHI 2013; Tuch et al.: complexity drives the 50ms impression

findings.title: Inter for 93% of the text
findings.evidence: Primary family is Inter, one of the fonts generated UIs default to. Fonts seen: Inter, Fraunces.
findings.fix: Not wrong on its own. If everything else is default too, this is the cheapest thing to change: pick one typeface with a point of view for headings and keep the workhorse for body.
findings.citation: Impeccable overused-font; HN thread on vibe-coded tells (Inter everywhere)

findings.title: Eyebrow label above the hero headline
findings.evidence: “Wayne · Pulaski · McCreary · Clinton Counties” (11px, tracked caps) sits directly above a 60px h1. The tiny label + giant headline pairing is the default generated SaaS hero.
findings.fix: Fold the label into the headline or the first sentence. If it's an announcement, make it a real link somewhere else.

findings.title: 3 untouched shadcn/ui cards
findings.evidence: Class strings like “rounded-xl border bg-card text-card-foreground shadow” are the component library's defaults, unmodified. Fine as scaffolding; as the final look it's tell #1.
findings.fix: Change the tokens (radius, border colour, shadow) once in your theme so the components stop looking like the docs page.

findings.title: 10 tracked all-caps section labels
findings.evidence: Small uppercase, letter-spaced labels like “Quotes” above sections. On 10.5% of Show HN launches, and usually redundant with the heading under them.
findings.fix: Delete the label or fold its word into the heading.

findings.title: Head is missing: canonical
findings.evidence: No JSON-LD structured data either, so AI search engines have nothing to cite. 2 h1 elements; use one.
findings.fix: Ten minutes of <head> work: title under 60 chars, canonical URL, lang attribute, favicon, and an Organization or WebSite JSON-LD block.

findings.title: Only 29% of the first screen is breathing room
findings.evidence: Pixels close to the page background make up less than a third of the viewport.
findings.fix: Widen margins and loosen section padding; comprehension measurably improves when content is framed by empty space (Lin 2004).
